key_insight: A four-network AI ensemble graded Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images with 85.0% accuracy, and all grading errors were between adjacent grades.
clinical_relevance: The model could support more consistent fibrosis grading in endemic areas with limited sonographer expertise, pending external validation.
method: Analyzed one B-mode ultrasound image per adult without manual region-of-interest delineation.
Combined ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T using validation-weighted soft voting.
Predicted four fibrosis grades using reference labels reviewed by radiologists.
evidence_signal: Using 2,921 adults from one hospital in China, the model achieved macro-F1 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184–0.8856) on a fixed 440-image test set and AUROC 0.9817 for grade 2–3 fibrosis.
watch_item: Single-hospital evaluation leaves generalizability to other populations, ultrasound equipment and clinical workflows unproven.
paper_title: Deep learning grading of Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images: a weighted soft-voting ensemble of convolutional and transformer networks
